answer: A market storing falcon telemetry, comet images, and orchard maps can allocate credits per verified byte instead of per account. Require replicas encoded for a specific owner key, then challenge random blocks under deadlines too short to regenerate the encoding. A storage proof must establish that different keys cannot cheaply share one replica. Splitting into aliases adds no free capacity: each extra credit requires more disk space, retrieval bandwidth, and power. Security depends on sound replication proofs and realistic deadlines.
